terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms cover using Tably: the owner and staff apps, the guest menu reached from a table's QR code, and this website. By using Tably you agree to them.

what.p: It is free to use and offered as it is, to show how restaurant and café ordering can work. It is not a paid service and comes with no service-level commitment.

items.a: Owners create an account with their full name, email and a password, and keep the details accurate.
items.b: Owners create the staff accounts for their business and are responsible for who gets one.
items.c: Keep your password to yourself. Tell us straight away if you think someone else has used your account.
items.d: We can suspend or close an account that breaks these terms.

demo.p: The demo account is shared: anyone can sign in and change its menu, tables, orders and bookings. Don't enter real personal details there. Its data can be reset at any time.

data.p: The menu, tables, orders, bookings, images and settings you add stay yours. Tably only uses them to run the service for you. If you connect your own database, real-time (Pusher) app or image storage, those services' own terms apply to them, and you're responsible for your accounts there.

guests.p: Guests order through the business, not through Tably. The business sets its menu, prices and taxes, and handles service and payment. Questions about an order go to the restaurant or café.

items.a: Don't use Tably for anything unlawful.
items.b: Don't try to reach another business's data, break the service or overload it.
items.c: Only upload images and text you have the right to use.

liability.p: Tably can change, pause or stop at any time. It is provided without warranties, and as far as the law allows, {{name}} isn't liable for lost data, lost orders or lost income from using it. Keep your own records of anything your business depends on.

changes.p: When these terms change, the date at the top changes too. See also the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> and <cookies>cookie policy</cookies>. Questions: <email>{{email}}</email>.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: What Tably collects, why, and who else handles it. Tably is run by {{name}}, who you can reach at {{email}}.

items.owners: Owner accounts: full name, email and password. Passwords are stored only as a bcrypt hash, never as you typed them.
items.staff: Staff accounts: the name, email and password an owner sets for each staff member.
items.business: Business data: menu, prices, tables, orders, bookings, settings, the logo and dish photos. Bookings hold the guest name and phone number staff enter.
items.guests: Guests at a table: no account and no personal details. Orders and requests such as “call staff” are tied to the table, not to a person.
items.messages: Messages: the name, email and message you send with a contact form.
items.usage: Usage: anonymous page-view counts from Vercel Analytics, which uses no cookies.

items.a: To sign you in and run your business's tables, orders and bookings.
items.b: To email the site owner about new sign-ups and contact messages, so they can reply.
items.c: To see which pages are used and improve them.

why.after: We don't sell your data or use it for advertising.

items.a: Vercel hosts the website, its analytics and, unless you connect your own, image storage.
items.b: Pusher delivers live updates, such as a new order reaching the staff screens.
items.c: Resend delivers the sign-up and contact-form emails.
items.d: If an owner connects their own database, Pusher app or image storage, that business's data is kept there instead.

keep.p: Account and business data are kept while the account exists. Contact messages stay in the site owner's inbox. The shared demo account can be reset at any time.

choices.p: To see, correct or delete your data, or to close your account, email <email>{{email}}</email>. Owners can edit or remove their staff accounts in the Staff tab. For what's stored in your browser, see the <cookies>cookie policy</cookies>.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: Tably sets only the cookies it needs to sign you in and to remember your language. There are no advertising or tracking cookies, so there's nothing to accept or turn off.

rows.session: Keeps you signed in. Removed when you sign out or the session ends.
rows.csrf: Protects the sign-in form from forged requests.
rows.callback: Remembers the page to return to after signing in.
rows.lang: The language you chose (English or Tiếng Việt). Kept for a year.
rows.signInAs: Whether you last signed in as Owner or Staff.
rows.sidebar: Whether you collapsed the app's sidebar.
rows.paper: The receipt paper width you print on (80 or 58 mm).
rows.building: That you've seen the workspace setup animation. Cleared when the tab closes.

cookies.p: Set by Auth.js when you sign in to the owner or staff app, plus lang when you pick a language. Guests ordering from a table get only lang, and only if they pick one. On a secure (https) connection the sign-in cookies' names start with __Secure- or __Host-.

storage.p: A few preferences are kept in your browser's own storage. They never leave your device and aren't sent to us.

analytics.p: Vercel Analytics counts page views without cookies and without identifying you.

control.p: You can clear or block cookies and site data in your browser settings. Blocking the session cookie means you can't sign in. More on what we collect is in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

form.noKey: The server can't store credentials yet (CREDENTIALS_KEY isn't set). Ask whoever runs this app to add it.
form.notConnected: Not connected: using the shared service.
form.databaseHelp: Use an empty database; we create the tables. A pooled URL works best (Neon, Supabase and Prisma Postgres all offer one).
form.databaseSwitch: Switching databases doesn't move your existing menu, orders or bookings.
form.pasteHelp: In your Pusher Channels app, open App Keys, click Copy and paste here to fill the fields below. Or type them in yourself.
form.pasteNone: Couldn't find Pusher credentials in that text. Copy them from your app's App Keys page.
form.storageHelp: Where dish photos and your logo are stored. It must allow public reads, since guests' browsers load the images.
form.storageSwitch: Switching storage doesn't move images already uploaded.
form.blobHelp: In Vercel, open Storage, pick your public Blob store and copy BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN from its .env.local tab.
form.s3Help: Works with AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Supabase Storage and MinIO. On AWS, the endpoint is https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com and the region is required. The public URL is the address the bucket's files are served from.
form.checkNote: All three are checked now (storage with a small test file, deleted again) and saved once your business is created in the next step.
form.saveNote: All three are checked before anything is saved (storage with a small test file, deleted again).
form.secretsNote: Passwords and secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again.
